key_insight: SeeThrough3D explicitly models inter-object occlusions in 3D layout-conditioned text-to-image generation, enabling synthesis of partially occluded objects with depth-consistent geometry and correct scale. This occlusion-aware conditioning closes a key gap where prior layout-based methods produced inconsistent occlusions and depth artifacts.
problem_solved: Existing 3D layout-conditioned generators often fail to reason about precise inter-object occlusions, producing objects that violate depth ordering, incorrect partial visibility, and inconsistent scale when placed in multi-object scenes.
method: Introduce an occlusion-aware 3D scene representation and a differentiable compositing module that encodes object depth, visibility ordering, and partial coverage.
Condition a text-to-image generative model on the 3D layout plus explicit occlusion/depth maps so the generator synthesizes objects with correct partial visibility and scale.
Optimize with depth- and occlusion-consistency objectives (and layout-aligned supervision) to enforce geometry-aware, occlusion-correct synthesis across scenes.
impact: Makes layout-conditioned image generation far more reliable for multi-object scenes by ensuring depth-consistent, realistically occluded outputs — useful for content creation, AR/VR, simulation, and any pipeline needing controllable scene composition.

paper_title: SeeThrough3D: Occlusion Aware 3D Control in Text-to-Image Generation
paper_authors: Vaibhav Agrawal, Rishubh Parihar, Pradhaan Bhat, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla, R. Venkatesh Babu
